15:
16:    Input structure
17:    - The grid has one dominant background color and one foreground wall color.
18:    - The wall pixels form one or more 4-connected one-cell-thick segments.
19:    - Each wall segment separates exactly two 4-connected background regions.
20:    Rule
21:    - Keep all wall pixels unchanged.
22:    - Label the 4-connected background regions and connect two labels when they
23:      touch opposite sides of the same wall segment.
24:    - Color the region containing the lower-left corner grey, then flip between
25:      grey and green across every wall adjacency.
26:    Key insight
27:    - The red walls define a bipartite map of regions; the lower-left background
28:      region fixes which side of the alternating coloring is grey.
29:    """
30:    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
31:    assert g.ndim == 2
32:    H, W = g.shape
33:
34:    colors = set(map(int, g.flat))
35:    assert len(colors) == 2, "expected exactly one background color and one wall color"
36:    bg = get_bg(g)
37:    wall_colors = colors - {int(bg)}
38:    assert len(wall_colors) == 1
39:    wall = int(next(iter(wall_colors)))

41:    bg_lab, n_regions = label_mask(g == int(bg), connectivity=4)
42:    assert n_regions >= 2, "walls must split the background into multiple regions"
43:    start_region = int(bg_lab[H - 1, 0])
44:    assert start_region > 0, "lower-left corner must belong to a background region"
45:
46:    wall_lab, n_walls = label_mask(g == wall, connectivity=4)
47:    assert n_walls >= 1
48:
49:    graph: dict[int, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
50:    for wall_id in range(1, n_walls + 1):
51:        adjacent_regions: set[int] = set()
52:        for r, c in np.argwhere(wall_lab == wall_id):
53:            for rr, cc in neighbors4(int(r), int(c)):
54:                if 0 <= rr < H and 0 <= cc < W:
55:                    region_id = int(bg_lab[rr, cc])
56:                    if region_id > 0:
57:                        adjacent_regions.add(region_id)
58:
59:        assert len(adjacent_regions) == 2, "each wall segment must separate exactly two regions"
60:        a, b = tuple(adjacent_regions)
61:        graph[a].add(b)
62:        graph[b].add(a)

64:    parity = {start_region: 0}
65:    queue = deque([start_region])
66:    while queue:
67:        region = queue.popleft()
68:        for neighbor in graph[region]:

70:            if neighbor in parity:
